nodes.label: select.ts
nodes.text: Hero: an Excel-style selection box (2px border and a fill handle) lands on "A1", then slides to "AI" while the CSS reel rolls 1 → I (design/README.md §5). The wordmark itself is CSS only and complete without this. The box is an absolutely positioned element moved with x/y (transforms) and sized with width/height, so it never shifts layout. It follows the CSS intro's own clock, so a chunk that arrives mid-intro joins in sync; one that arrives after the roll only fades the box in on "AI" and never replays the intro. The CSS intro clock (home.css): box on A1 at BOX_IN, slide in sync with the reel roll. Seconds. Both boxes, in the wordmark's own (unscaled) pixels. Rows come from the A1 mask, which the entrance never transforms; columns of AI come from its own rect, which the rise (translateY, skewY) leaves unchanged horizontally. k undoes the hero's scroll-out scale, if the page is already scrolled. / Seconds since the CSS intro started: the reel animation's start time when known, else navigation start. late: the CSS roll has already ended, so the box simply appears where it ends up Size changes (rotation, zoom, the web font arriving): finish in place, or carry on from the same moment…

nodes.label: gsap.ts
nodes.text: Single entry to GSAP for the homepage. Imported only from the deferred motion chunks, so the library never sits on the critical path. Plugins are registered by the modules that use them. No ticker.fps() cap and the default lagSmoothing: the ticker follows requestAnimationFrame, so tweens run at the display's refresh rate (120 Hz phones included). The brand ease: the same curve as `--ease` in home.css (the CSS intro), so a CSS entrance and a GSAP one land identically. Used as 'dfz' by every section. The mobile address bar resizing the viewport must not trigger a refresh while scrolling. Read-before-write for a batch of targets. GSAP reads an element's computed transform the first time it animates it, and every read after a write forces a style recalculation. Priming the caches of all targets first turns N interleaved read/write pairs into N reads in a row (one recalculation) followed by pure writes. / Run a timeline to its end and back to where it was. GSAP reads a tween's start values (computed styles, SVG path lengths) the first time it renders, which for a scrubbed timeline would be mid-scroll, in a frame the reader sees; this does it now, in a setup slot. nodes.label: history-curve.ts
nodes.text: The history slider's look as a function of a card's distance from the center (in cards), shared by the CSS first frame (components/home/History.astro, built at build time) and the GSAP loop (sections/history.ts), so the two always agree. No GSAP here: this module is also imported at build time. Cards move 80% of their width per step; one card's whole pass (400% → -400%) is ±5 steps. Opacity by distance, at |d| = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Scale and opacity are separate: the neighbors at ±1 stay at 0.9, so their smallest text (--soft) keeps 4.5:1 in both themes (dark about 7:1, light about 5.4:1); from ±2 the cards fade out. / u: 1 at the center, 0 at the ends of the pass (|d| = 5). Opacity for a position on the pass (piecewise linear through OPACITY). Used as a GSAP ease. Scale for a position on the pass: power1.in, as in the GSAP demo. The same two values for a whole-card distance (the CSS first frame).

nodes.label: motion.ts
nodes.text: Deferred homepage motion: nav, scroll progress, hero scroll-out, pointer effects, and the section timelines. Everything is inside gsap.matchMedia(), so reduced motion gets none of it (and in practice never even loads this chunk). Frame budget (SPEC §12, 8.3 ms at 120 Hz): per-frame work is O(1) and touches only transform and opacity. Sizes are measured once and again on ScrollTrigger's refresh, never inside a tween, and writes happen in GSAP's own rAF tick. Setup work (the section timelines) is split into one task per section and runs right after a presented frame, first for sections near the screen, then, while the reader is not scrolling, for the rest, so scrolling never pays for it. The history list (04) keeps the slider's height while it waits for its chunk: if the chunk cannot build the slider, the list takes its own height again. `all` also resets a slider whose setup failed halfway. / One unit of setup work: a section's init, or one of the later steps it asked for (see SectionInit). Section name, to find its effect loader (see sections/index.ts). Fetching the section's effect chunks (MotionPath, Flip, Draggable, ...), started when the job is near or due. After the CSS intro…

DrawSVG end states use 102%: Firefox can measure path length slightly short and leave a gap at 100%. 02: one scrubbed timeline builds the tree while the sticky stage holds (CSS), or plays in flow on short screens. Reads first, then the writes: one style recalculation instead of one per element. Built first, linked to the scroll last (see the final step), so it is complete and initialized early by the time the reader can move it. The rest are steps (a task each), so no single task is long. tl.to({}, { duration: 0.8 }); // hold the finished tree for a beat before the stage releases the tree repaints every frame while it draws: give it its own layer for exactly that long path lengths depend on size: re-measure after a refresh, in a setup slot (see initAgainOnRefresh) the lights get a task of their own: MotionPath measures every path when it is first rendered every branch has drawn at (label + draw time + the last stagger)

One card's pass across the stage: it slides from 400% to -400% of its width while it grows to full size at the center and shrinks again (power1.in both ways). Opacity has its own curve (history-curve.ts): the neighbors stay readable, the cards further out fade. Transforms and opacity only. / The seamless loop of the GSAP "Infinite card slider" demo: every card's pass is laid out on a raw timeline, SPACING apart, with extra copies before and after so that every moment of the loop has its neighbors on both sides. A second timeline scrubs a window of exactly one lap of the raw one and repeats forever, so time t centers card t / SPACING and the end of the lap is the same picture as its start. nodes.label: index.ts
nodes.text: One deferred module for every section timeline (a single request). motion.ts builds each section in its own task: near the screen first, the rest once the intro is over and the reader is not scrolling. A later piece of a section's setup, run in a frame slot of its own (keeps every task short). Builds a section. A heavy one may return the rest of its work as steps instead of doing it all at once. Fetches the effect chunks a section uses on top of its base timeline (one dynamic import per plugin group). motion.ts starts it when the section is near the screen and waits for it before building, so the section is built once, with the effects in hand; a failed fetch skips only those effects. /

nodes.text: Flip moves the tab underline; its own chunk, fetched when the section is near. How long each tool stays on screen while the tabs cycle by themselves. 03: on every tab change the underline slides (Flip, transforms only), the code fades up and the result rows pulse, because the answer is the same each time. The tabs cycle by themselves only while the section is on screen, and stop for good once the reader touches the widget (click, key, focus, hover); a small Pause / Play button controls the cycle (WCAG 2.2.2). Reduced motion never loads this: the tabs still work. / Auto-cycle: runs while on screen, unless the reader paused it or used the tabs. The label states the action; no aria-pressed, which would contradict it (WCAG 4.1.2). if (!stopped) t.select(t.index + 1, 'auto'); // resume visibly, then every CYCLE_MS

nodes.label: tabs.ts
nodes.text: Homepage section 03: the stacked solutions become an ARIA tab list (WAI-ARIA APG "Tabs", automatic activation): roving tabindex, ←/→ (wrapping), Home and End. No GSAP and no motion: home-boot.ts loads this for every reader once the page is idle, reduced motion included. The deferred motion chunk (sections/tools.ts) hooks into `before` / `after` for the animation and the auto-cycle. Panels share one grid cell, so the widget is as tall as its tallest panel: switching tabs never moves the page (CLS 0, also when the auto-cycle switches). Runs before the change is written (Flip reads its state here). panel.tabIndex = 0; // a code panel has nothing focusable inside: the panel itself takes focus

nodes.label: yield.ts
nodes.text: Scheduling helper for setup work. The rule: none of our tasks runs inside a frame the reader is scrolling through, so each heavy step starts right after a frame has been presented. Resolves in the first task after the next frame's rendering: requestAnimationFrame runs before the frame's style, layout and paint, and the timeout fires after them. A step started here gets a fresh frame budget. (scheduler.yield() alone resumes before the next render, so a chain of yields still adds up to one long animation frame.) /

nodes.label: taskbar.ts
nodes.text: The bottom taskbar (SPEC D31): the only script on project, lesson and reference pages, under 1 KB gzipped. No library and no animation here: the motion is CSS transitions (none under reduced motion). - the shortcuts sheet: aria-expanded, inert while closed; Esc, a second tap, a link or an outside click closes it, and Esc returns focus to the button; - the theme switch: Starlight's own state (data-theme on <html>, localStorage `starlight-theme`), so the homepage and the docs agree; dark unless the reader chose light; - back-to-top is dimmed near the top; - on the homepage, the label names the section on screen ([data-tb-name]). Storage can be blocked: the choice then lasts for this page view. The first reads of style and scroll position wait for the first frame, so they never force the page's first layout early.
